question: Pursuant to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/297, imports of silicomanganese steel wire covered by anti-dumping investigation AD746 have been subject to mandatory registration since 11 February 2026. This measure is causing considerable uncertainty for importers and companies using this product as a key raw material, particularly in the construction, automotive and heavy industry sectors.
Of particular concern is the possibility of the retroactive collection of duties, which could jeopardise the liquidity of SMEs and affect the continuity of supply. With the above in mind: 1.

How does the Commission assess the likelihood of anti-dumping duties being imposed retroactively for the period covered by mandatory registration, and what criteria will determine the application of this measure?
When will investigation AD746 be concluded and any interim measures published?

How does the Commission intend to weigh, in the Union interest test, the impact of any duties on the competitiveness of EU industry and the situation of SMEs that depend on stable supplies of welding wire?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.9.2026) To apply duties retroactively, the Commission is bound by Article 10(4) of the basic Antidumping Regulation1.

There should be a further substantial rise in imports in addition to the level of imports which caused injury during the investigation period which, in the light of its timing and volume and other circumstances, is likely to seriously undermine the remedial effect of the definitive anti-dumping duty to be applied. The provisional measures were published on 10 August 20262.

Pre-disclosure of the level of intended provisional measures has been communicated to parties on 13 July 2026. At the initiation of the investigation, the Commission invited all known users of welding wire to cooperate in the investigation. Until now, no user came forward. However, users can still register as interested party in the investigation and submit comments at a later stage.
If no users cooperate, findings with regard to the EU interest will be based on the complaint and information obtained at EU producers, exporting producers, and unrelated importers.
